theater: 尼尼微城與底格里斯河東岸

battle.name: 尼尼微戰役
battle.theater: 尼尼微城與底格里斯河東岸
battle.brief: 公元前612年，基亞克薩列斯的米底軍與拿波那帕沙的巴比倫軍聯手攻亞述都城：先取阿卡德與西帕爾，五月進抵尼尼微，圍城約三個月。西城牆一段被地道夜襲攻破，聯軍入城焚燒王宮、掠走神像，末代王阿舒爾-巴尼拔二世逃往哈蘭。城頭最後一道防線由亞述長矛與弓箭構成。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries:
公元前612年攻破尼尼微的聯軍由兩個新生的國家組成：美索不達米亞南方的迦勒底新巴比倫王國，與伊朗高原北部的米底王國。巴比倫一方由國王拿波那帕沙（Nabopolassar，前626至前605年在位）直接統帥。迦勒底人原是亞述西部的行省民族，前7世紀末亞述曾派兵平定巴比倫「海上之國」地區以辛馬爾舒姆烏金為首的反叛，其後亞述王權在這裡又維持了二十餘年；前626年拿波那帕沙即位時，巴比倫已完全脫離亞述。巴比倫王室的官方說法把迦勒底王朝說成亞述王族的旁支，拿波那帕沙以亞述王統的正統繼承者自居，這一點成為他後來瓜分亞述疆域的政治資本。他的軍隊以步兵與弓手為骨幹，攻城器械齊備，斜坡、撞柱與護牆都是長期累積的經驗；軍官多出身迦勒底氏族，軍中按名冊發給口糧與兵器，士卒的組成相當雜。

米底一方由國王基亞克薩列斯（Cyaxares）率領，即後來被希臘人稱為阿斯提亞格斯者。米底人於前7世紀中葉趁亞述遠征埃及、國力空虛時脫離亞述，前625年前後建國，都城在哈爾克（Ecbatana，今哈馬丹），國勢的核心在裏海西南岸的低地。米底的軍隊組織與亞述全然不同：全國分為許多大小不一的部落，每部之下設有「薩卡帕蒂」（sakapatis）等作戰單位，兵種以弓手與騎兵為主，騎射是米底人最看家的本事，馬上挽弓、縱馬衝陣是制勝法寶。基亞克薩列斯的功勞在於把互不相屬的部落綁成聯盟，設盟主、供軍賦，戰時他駐節哈爾克，主要戰線交給前線將領指揮，這與亞述那種王權高度集中、國王親臨前線的體制截然不同。

亞述一方則已是一個空心化的帝國。末代之王阿舒爾-巴尼拔二世在位不過兩三年，疆域縮到上美索不達米亞一隅，王室靠正規的「國王之兵」、王宮近衛，以及改編自被鎮壓部落的徵發兵勉力支撐，士氣與裝備都遠不及全盛期。聯軍之中還有數量可觀的西徐亞騎兵，這支部族活動於黑海北岸，是聯軍中機動性最強的一翼。亞述一方真正可恃的，是尼尼微這座以鐵器、投石機與高大城牆武裝到牙齒的都城，以及城牆上那支仍握著短柄長矛的老軍。
countriesEn: The coalition that broke Nineveh in 612 BC was made up of two newborn states: the Chaldean Neo-Babylonian kingdom in the southern Mesopotamian plain, and the Median kingdom in the north of the Iranian plateau. The Babylonian side was commanded directly by the king, Nabopolassar (r. 626 to 605 BC). The Chaldeans had originally been a subject people of western Assyria; in the late seventh century BC Assyria sent an army to put down the revolt in the Sea Land district of Babylonia led by Sîn-mâr-šum-ukin, and the Assyrian king then kept its grip on the city for another two decades or more. When Nabopolassar took the throne in 626 BC, Babylonia had already broken away from Assyria altogether. The official Babylonian line of descent made the Chaldean dynasty a cadet branch of the Assyrian royal house, and Nabopolassar presented himself as the legitimate heir of the Assyrian kings; that claim became the political capital with which he would later carve up Assyrian territory. His army had infantry and archers as its backbone, and was well supplied with siege equipment, ramps, battering rams and outworks, all of it the accumulated experience of long campaigns against places like Akkad and Kish. His officers came largely from Chaldean clans, and the army was administered through nominal rolls, with rations and weapons issued by name. The Median side was led by the king Cyaxares, the man the Greeks later called Astyages. The Medes had broken away from Assyria in the middle of the seventh century BC, while Assyria was bogged down in Egypt and its strength was elsewhere, and they set up their kingdom around 625 BC with its capital at Ecbatana, the modern Hamadan, the core of their power lying in the lowlands to the south-west of the Caspian. Their military organisation was nothing like the Assyrian one: the country was divided into a great many tribes of unequal size, each subdivided into fighting units the Greeks call sakapatis, and the arms of the service were archers and horsemen, with mounted archery their strongest and most characteristic technique, the shot loosed from the saddle at the gallop. Cyaxares' achievement was to bind unrelated tribes into a league with a leader and a war levy; he himself sat at Ecbatana and left the main front to his commanders in the field, a system wholly unlike the Assyrian one, where kingship was highly concentrated and the king fought in person at the head of the army. The Assyrian side, meanwhile, was an empire hollowed out. Its last king, Ashur-uballit II, held the throne for two or three years at most; the realm had shrunk to the upper Mesopotamian corner, and the court was sustained by the regular royal army, the palace guard and levies remade from populations it had already suppressed, all of them lower in morale and worse equipped than in the empire's prime. The coalition also contained a substantial body of Scythian horsemen, a people living north of the Black Sea and the most mobile wing of the invading force. What Assyria could still rely on was Nineveh itself, a capital armoured with iron, artillery and towering walls, and the old troops on those walls still holding their short-hafted spears.
people:
本役留下名字的人不多，但每一位都在關鍵位置上。第一位是拿波那帕沙，前626年即位、前605年去世，是這場戰爭的策劃者與巴比倫方面的總指揮。他不是以蠻力取勝的君主，而是把「亞述的正統繼承人」這張牌打到極致的人：前612年他聯手米底，奪取亞述西部的阿卡德與西帕爾，把聯軍推到尼尼微城下；城破後他沒有急著吞下整個上美索不達米亞，而是先把重心放在西界，於前609年攻陷哈蘭。他後來在對米底的戰役中死去，聯盟的破裂也隨之而來。

第二位是基亞克薩列斯，即後來被希臘人稱為阿斯提亞格斯的那位米底王。他的角色是把一群各自獨立的部落變成聯軍：出兵、出賦、出騎兵，並且承擔了聯軍最重的一段行軍與騎射作戰。希羅多德把尼尼微的陷落單獨記在米底名下，甚至說城是被米底人攻破的，亞述王也在那一戰中陣亡；巴比倫編年史則把同一件事記成兩國聯軍的共同行動，並提到亞述王在城破時不在其中。這兩種說法的分歧，說明希臘傳統把米底的功勞放大、把巴比倫的作用抹去，而巴比倫的泥板則以自己的政治語言陳述聯軍的功勞。

第三位是阿舒爾-巴尼拔二世，亞述王朝的最後一位君王，在位約前611至前609年。他在亞述巴尼拔一世（即以獅獵浮雕與圖書館著稱的亞述巴尼拔，前668至前631年在位）與辛沙里施昆之後接位，接手的是一個只剩上美索不達米亞的殘破帝國；前612年城破時他不在城中被擒，而是帶著王室殘部逃往西北的哈蘭，在那裡又據守兩年，前609年哈蘭陷落後才輾轉西走，投奔埃及法老普桑提克二世，最後死於流亡。亞述王室的徹底結束，是在哈蘭而不是在尼尼微。

另有拿波尼idus，拿波那帕沙之子、末代巴比倫王，此時已被派往阿拉伯半島的泰瑪綠洲作戰，他的編年史記載了同一時期聯軍如何瓜分尼尼微的戰利品與神像，後來他即位的圓柱銘文也回述了這段戰史。尼布甲尼撒繼承人阿米爾-馬爾杜克則是聯盟瓦解後的關鍵人物：前605年他在卡爾迪希一役擊敗米底，把亞述故地大部收入巴比倫版圖。希羅多德書中那段著名插話裡的魚市婦人，也常被後世拿來說明攻城戰的細節。
peopleEn: Few names survive from this campaign, but every one of them stood in a decisive position. The first is Nabopolassar, who reigned from 626 to 605 BC and who was both the author of the war and the commander on the Babylonian side. He was not a ruler who won by brute force; he pushed the card of legitimate heir of Assyria to its limit. In 612 BC he joined hands with the Medes, took the Assyrian cities of Akkad and Sippar in the west, and drove the coalition up to the walls of Nineveh. After the city's fall he did not rush to swallow the whole of upper Mesopotamia; he weighted his position toward the western border instead and took Harran in 609 BC. He died later in a war against the Medes, and the alliance fell apart with him. The second is Cyaxares, the Median king whom the Greeks came to call Astyages. His task was to turn a set of independent tribes into a coalition: to provide men, money and cavalry, and to carry the heaviest share of the marching and of the mounted archery. Herodotus records the fall of Nineveh as the work of the Medes alone, and even has the Assyrian king killed in that battle, while the Babylonian chronicle sets down the same event as the joint work of the two countries and notes that the Assyrian king was not in the city when it was taken. The divergence between the two accounts shows the Greek tradition magnifying the Medes' credit and erasing the Babylonian role, while the Babylonian tablets state the coalition's achievement in their own political language. The third figure is Ashur-uballit II, the last king of the Assyrian dynasty, who reigned from about 611 to 609 BC. He succeeded Ashurbanipal I and Sîn-šhar-ishkun and inherited a broken empire reduced to upper Mesopotamia; when the city fell in 612 BC he was not captured in it, but escaped with the remnants of the court to Harran in the north-west, held out there for two more years, and after Harran fell in 609 BC made his way west to the court of the Egyptian pharaoh Psamtik II, where he died in exile. The Assyrian royal house was ended at Harran, not at Nineveh. There is also Nabonidus, son of Nabopolassar and last king of Babylon, then dispatched to the oasis of Tema in Arabia; his chronicle records how the coalition divided the spoil and the gods of Nineveh, and the cylinder inscription of his later reign looks back on the same campaign. Amel-Marduk, who succeeded Nabopolassar, is the decisive figure in the break-up of the alliance: in 605 BC he defeated the Medes at Cadytia and brought most of the former Assyrian lands into the Babylonian empire. And the fishwife of the fish market, in the famous episode of Herodotus, is often invoked for what she shows about the detail of siege warfare.
kits:
本卡所示的亞述長矛，是新亞述軍隊近戰的骨幹：短柄、長刃、鐵鏃，握在手中配一面可立於身前的長方大盾，列成三排密集的矛陣前推，盾與矛同時起作用，箭手則在矛陣之後成排齊射。這件兵器在尼尼微攻防中的位置十分明確：城頭上，長矛手與弓手交替掩護，構成對付攻城塔與雲梯的最後一道近戰線；城門與缺口處，矛陣要承受的是密集的撞柱與攀城者。亞述的長矛並非孤立的技術亮點，而是整套新亞述裝備體系的尖端的鐵器技術這一環，箭鏃、刀劍、斧與投槍都可以在同一條冶鐵產線上大量生產。

聯軍方面的裝備與亞述不同。米底騎兵用短而有力的弓，箭鏃有鐵製也有骨製，數量極大，靠騎射在攻城階段覆蓋城牆；巴比倫步兵則以弓手見長，弓身更長、拉力更大、箭程更遠，箭雨密度是兩河流域諸國之最，長矛與槍在正面，弓在側翼與後方。攻城器械是巴比倫的看家本領：撞柱用木樑包銅反覆撞擊門扇，斜坡以土築成、覆生牛皮以防火燒，掘進的地道沿牆基挖入，希羅多德記載的那段地道夜襲正是靠這種工事達成的。與此同時，圍城方還要處理水源與糧食：亞述城內有自西南二十餘公里外霍斯爾河引水入城的水渠，是西拿希里布時期開鑿、修於前7世紀的工程，因此守軍並不缺水，圍城方無法以斷水取勝，只能破門。

運輸方面，聯軍依靠底格里斯河的水運把糧秣從西帕爾、阿卡德一線運到軍營，再以騾車、牛車轉運到陣地；亞述一方的補給靠城內屯糧與行省徵發。攻城方必須在盛夏的酷熱中維持三個月的營地，疾病與缺糧是比攻城武器更實際的威脅，而亞述守軍倚靠城內儲備與水渠，時間站在城牆一邊。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear shown on this card was the backbone of close combat in the Neo-Assyrian army: a short shaft, a long blade and an iron head, carried together with a tall rectangular shield that could be set on the ground in front of the man, so that the front ranks advanced with spear and shield working as one while archers behind them fired in volleys. The weapon's place in the defence of Nineveh is plain enough: on the walls, spearmen and archers covered one another in turn and formed the last close-combat line against siege towers and ladders; at the gates and in the breaches, the spear line had to absorb the shock of the battering rams and of the men climbing the wall. The Assyrian spear was not an isolated technical flourish but the sharp end of a complete system, and its edge was the iron technology at the tip of that system: arrowheads, blades, axes and javelins could all be produced in bulk along the same iron-working lines. The coalition's equipment was different in character. The Median horse used short, powerful bows with iron and bone arrowheads in great numbers, covering the walls with fire from the saddle throughout the siege. Babylonian infantry were outstanding as archers, with a longer bow of greater draw and longer reach than the Assyrian one and the highest density of arrows in Mesopotamia; spears and javelins went in front, bows on the flanks and behind. Siege engineering was the Babylonian speciality: battering rams with bronze-bound beams struck the gate leaves again and again, ramps were built of earth and covered with rawhide against the fire, and tunnels were driven in along the foot of the wall. The night assault by tunnel that Herodotus describes was achieved by exactly this kind of work. At the same time the besiegers had to solve water and food: Nineveh's own aqueduct, cut in the reign of Sennacherib in the seventh century BC, drew water from the Khosr river some twenty kilometres to the south-west, so the defenders were not short of water and the siege could not be won by cutting the supply; the wall had to be broken. On the logistics side, the coalition brought grain and stores up the Tigris by water from the line of Sippar and Akkad and then carried them to the camps by mule and ox cart, while Assyria's own supply rested on the grain stored in the city and on requisition from the provinces. The besiegers had to hold their camps through three months of high summer, and sickness and hunger were a more practical threat than any siege engine; the defenders, with the city's stores and its aqueduct, had time on their side.
tactics:
這是一場典型的攻城戰，而攻城戰的全部難題都壓在西城牆上。聯軍的部署是多面的：西面壓住阿卡德門一段，南面封住通往阿卡德與西帕爾的道路，東面控制霍斯爾河與底格里斯河之間的通道，斷掉城內對外的交通，同時把營地與底格里斯河之間的取水路保持在手裡，防止亞述守軍切斷自己的水源。攻城不是一次撞門，而是多工種並進：工匠在前沿修築斜坡與護牆，工兵在牆基掘地道，弓手在後方以齊射壓制牆頭，迫得守軍把身位藏在垛口後面，撞柱則在斜坡頂端準備就緒，等待破門的一刻。

巴比倫編年史記載，圍城之中亞述守軍曾多次出城反擊，聯軍營地屢受襲擊而損失慘重，一度退卻重整，這說明聯軍的進攻並非一氣呵成，而是靠反覆衝擊把守軍的士氣與體力磨掉。希羅多德記錄了另一段細節：米底人先用強攻失利，其後在城外做工程，某夜由一名在城牆外擺賣魚鮮的婦人告知城牆有一段臨近魚市、修得較薄，聯軍遂以地道夜襲，奪下這一段牆面。總攻集中在塔穆茲月，聯軍由破口湧入，焚燒王宮、掠走神像與財物，並把俘獲的人口分給各部將領；城北的庫雲吉克王宮區與城南的納比尤努斯區在同一夜陷落。

守方的戰術則是以城牆代軍陣：亞述長矛手與弓手交替配置，把每一座城門、每一處垛口都當成射擊與刺擊的支點，以拒馬與門閂封住內門，用投石與射擊干擾填土的工兵，並趁夜出城襲營。密封的水渠與城內屯糧讓守軍有條件撐過三個月，但那三個月的消耗，最終還是被聯合軍隊的攻城技術與同盟結構壓垮。戰後的收尾仍在西北：前609年，哈蘭陷落，亞述王室的殘部連同最後的希望一併西遷埃及。
tacticsEn: This was a siege in the proper sense, and the whole difficulty of it pressed on the western wall. The coalition deployed on several faces: on the west they gripped the stretch of wall around the Akkadian gate, on the south they sealed the roads to Akkad and Sippar, on the east they held the corridor between the Khosr river and the Tigris and cut the city's outward traffic, while keeping the line of water from the Tigris to their own camps so that the defenders could not cut them off. The assault was not a single blow at the gate but a convergence of trades: engineers built ramps and outworks at the front, sappers drove tunnels along the foot of the wall, archers in the rear fired volleys to pin the defenders behind the crenellations and let the rams wait at the head of the ramp until the gate should break. The Babylonian chronicle records that the Assyrians sallied out more than once during the siege, that the coalition's camp was repeatedly struck and its losses heavy, and that the allies withdrew and re-formed at least once, which shows that the attack was not carried through in a single rush but ground down the defenders' morale and stamina by repeated blows. Herodotus preserves another piece of detail: the Medes first failed by assault and then set to work outside the walls, and one night a woman selling fish below the wall told them that one section of the circuit, near the fish market, had been built thin, so the besiegers came up through a tunnel and took that stretch of wall. The general assault came in the month of Tammuz; the coalition poured in through the breach, burned the palace, carried off the gods and the treasure, and allotted the prisoners to the commanders of the various contingents; the palace area of Kuyunjik in the north of the city and the quarter of Nabi Yunus in the south fell in the same night. The defence was the wall itself used in place of a battle line: Assyrian spearmen and archers were alternated so that every gate and every crenel became a post both for shooting and for stabbing, the inner doors were barred with crossbeams and spiked obstacles, missiles and arrows kept the filling crews of the ramp under constant harassment, and night sorties were made against the besiegers' camp. The sealed aqueduct and the grain in store allowed the defenders to hold out for three months, but the consumption of those three months was finally overcome by the besiegers' siege engineering and by the structure of their alliance. The mopping-up continued in the north-west: Harran fell in 609 BC, and what was left of the Assyrian royal house migrated west to Egypt with its last hope.
data: 可核對的數字分幾類。其一是年表：巴比倫編年史把聯軍奪取西帕爾與阿卡德記在沙巴圖月，把尼尼微的陷落記在塔穆茲月，即巴比倫曆第五月，換算成公曆約公元前612年七月初；圍城歷時約三個月，則對應五月進抵城下。聯軍在尼尼微以西的行程自巴比倫起算約七百公里，走底格里斯河與陸路並行。其二是城池的規格：尼尼微城牆周長約十二公里，牆高約十二至十五米、頂寬數米、底寬可達十米以上，外有寬約二十米的壕溝，城牆上開有十餘座城門，圍出的城區面積約十二平方公里；城內引水渠長二十餘公里，這些數字來自近代考古測量。其三是希臘史料的兵力記載：希羅多德《歷史》1.178至1.181與狄奧多羅斯《圖書集》2.21至2.23都給出十萬量級的聯軍與數萬守軍，但兩書的數字彼此不一致，也與巴比倫編年史的簡潔記載無法對應，學界普遍視為文學性的誇大；現代研究多認為聯軍總兵力在數萬量級，守軍當在數千至一萬之間。人口方面，尼尼微在前612年的城市人口沒有可靠記載，學者從城區面積與糧食供應反推的估計從數萬到二十餘萬不等，多屬推算而無文本依據。其四是考古與出土量：2012至2013年紐卡斯爾大學與愛丁堡大學的伊拉克團隊在尼尼微西城牆三門附近發掘，發現攻城破壞層、火燒痕跡與被毀的住宅區，出土數千件器物殘件，證實城破時曾縱火；19世紀由萊亞德與拉薩姆主持的發掘，則從城北王宮區取走亞述巴尼拔獅獵浮雕等大批青銅與象牙器，並在填土與坍塌層中挖出數以萬計的泥板，構成今日所謂的「亞述巴尼拔圖書館」。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into several classes. The first is the chronology: the Babylonian chronicle records the seizure of Sippar and Akkad in the month of Shabatu and the fall of Nineveh in the month of Tammuz, that is the fifth month of the Babylonian calendar, which converts to about early July 612 BC; the siege is said to have lasted about three months, which fits an advance to the walls in May. The distance the coalition covered from Babylon in the west of the siege is about seven hundred kilometres, part by river on the Tigris and part by road. The second class concerns the specifications of the city: the circuit of the walls of Nineveh ran to roughly twelve kilometres, the wall stood about twelve to fifteen metres high, several metres thick at the top and more than ten metres at the base, a moat about twenty metres wide ran outside it, the circuit carried a dozen or more gates, and the enclosed area came to about twelve square kilometres; the aqueduct that brought water into the city was over twenty kilometres long. These figures come from modern archaeological measurement. The third class is the Greek figures for the armies: Herodotus, Histories 1.178 to 1.181, and Diodorus, Bibliotheca 2.21 to 2.23, both give allied armies in the hundreds of thousands and defenders in the tens of thousands, but the two accounts do not agree with each other either, and they cannot be reconciled with the terse entries of the Babylonian chronicle; the general scholarly view is that they are literary exaggerations. Modern work puts the coalition's total force in the range of tens of thousands and the garrison somewhere between several thousand and ten thousand. On population there is no reliable figure for Nineveh in 612 BC; estimates drawn from the area of the city and from the food supply range from a few tens of thousands to more than two hundred thousand, and are in every case inference rather than text. The fourth class is archaeology and the volume of finds: between 2012 and 2013 a team from Newcastle University and the University of Edinburgh working with Iraqi colleagues excavated near Gate 3 on the western wall and uncovered a destruction layer, traces of burning and a wrecked residential quarter, with several thousand sherds and objects, confirming that the city was fired as it fell; and the nineteenth-century excavations directed by Layard and Rassam took from the northern palace area the great bronze and ivory reliefs, including the lion hunts of Ashurbanipal, and from the fill and collapsed masonry above them dug out tens of thousands of clay tablets, the collection known today as the Library of Ashurbanipal.
cause:
要理解這場戰爭為何會打成，須回到亞述帝國晚期。亞述在前7世紀把版圖推到埃及、伊朗高原、埃塞俄比亞與阿拉伯的邊緣，帝國的核心卻是上美索不達米亞一條狹長的河谷，維持這條河谷靠的是重稅、強行遷徙、地方鎮壓與不斷的遠征。壓力之下，反抗此起彼伏：巴比倫「海上之國」地區以辛馬爾舒姆烏金為首的反亂，前7世紀末被亞述平滅；被鎮壓的阿拉伯部落、埃及與埃塞俄比亞的臣屬也屢次叛離。亞述每一次鎮壓都加深了仇恨，也消耗了自己的元氣。

米底與巴比倫的獨立，是同一個真空的兩端。亞述前7世紀的遠征主力遠離本土時，米底在伊朗高原脫離亞述的宗主體系，前625年前後建國並重建軍制；巴比倫的迦勒底人則利用亞述內部的反亂與外部的干擾，在前626年把阿舒爾王朝的西界宗主權趕走。兩國都需要一位共同的反亞述盟友，因而在前7世紀末結成了同盟。

拿波那帕沙的王朝宣稱給這個同盟加上了政治色彩：他自稱亞述王族的合法繼承者，把「恢復秩序」與「報復亞述的暴政」捆在一起宣傳給西方諸國與行省。這既是招牌，也帶來約束：他不僅要推翻亞述王，還要接管亞述的行政與軍制，因為這些正是他新王國的運作基礎。

直接導火線是前612年的春季攻勢。聯軍先取阿卡德與西帕爾，切斷亞述在西南的門戶，然後直趨尼尼微；此時亞述新王即位未久，軍隊尚未整編，帝國能徵集的兵力與士氣都已遠低於前7世紀上半葉。一場原本屬於帝國內戰的危機，就此變成兩個聯盟國家瓜分亞述的戰爭。
causeEn: To understand why this war was fought, one has to go back to the late Assyrian empire. In the seventh century BC Assyria carried its territory to the edges of Egypt, the Iranian plateau, Ethiopia and Arabia, but the empire's core was the narrow river valley of upper Mesopotamia, and that valley was held down by heavy tribute, forced deportation, local repression and repeated distant campaigns. Under that pressure revolts kept coming: the rising in the Sea Land district of Babylonia led by Sîn-mâr-šum-ukin was put down in the late seventh century, and the Arab tribes it had suppressed, and the subject peoples of Egypt and Ethiopia, broke away again and again. Every suppression deepened the hatred and drained the empire's strength. The independence of Media and Babylonia was the two ends of the same vacuum. When Assyria's armies of the seventh century were far from home, the Medes broke loose from its lordship on the Iranian plateau and founded a kingdom with a rebuilt army around 625 BC; and the Chaldeans of Babylonia, exploiting the revolt inside Assyria and the pressure from outside, drove out the Assyrian suzerainty over the western frontier in 626 BC. Both countries needed a common ally against Assyria, and that is what bound them together in the late seventh century. Nabopolassar's dynastic claim gave the alliance its political colouring: he presented himself as the lawful heir of the Assyrian royal house and bound together the slogans of restoring order and avenging Assyrian tyranny, addressed to the western states and the provinces. That was at once a banner and a constraint, for he did not merely want to overthrow the Assyrian king; he wanted to take over the Assyrian administration and military system, because those were the working foundations of his own new kingdom. The immediate occasion was the spring offensive of 612 BC: the coalition took Akkad and Sippar, cut off Assyria's south-western door, and drove straight for Nineveh. The Assyrian king had by then been on the throne for only a short time, the army was not yet reformed, and the troops and morale the empire could still raise were far below those of the first half of the seventh century, and what had been a crisis internal to the empire turned into a war between two allied states to divide Assyria between them.
impact:
這場圍城的直接後果，是亞述帝國的終結。尼尼微陷落之後，亞述作為獨立的政治實體只剩下哈蘭一隅，前609年哈蘭亦落入巴比倫之手，王室西遷埃及；從此以後近東世界再也沒有一個獨立的亞述，直到19世紀萊亞德與拉薩姆在摩蘇爾的墳丘中挖出城牆與王宮，學界才重新知道有這麼一個帝國存在。

第二層影響是兩河流域權力格局的重排。巴比倫與米底在聯盟初期的目的是共同推翻亞述，卻在分贏的時候埋下分裂：巴比倫取得西部的哈蘭與下美索不達米亞，米底取得東北方的高地，前609年兩方在哈蘭一帶衝突，前605年巴比倫在卡爾迪希一役擊敗米底，聯盟徹底破裂，亞述故地大部落入巴比倫，尼布甲尼撒時代的「亞述行省」正是這樣變成巴比倫的一個行省。亞述的行政傳統、楔形文字文書體系與軍制沒有失傳，而是被繼承者整套吸收，這是帝國滅亡時常見的情形：統治的機器被拆開重裝。

第三層是知識與工藝的保存與轉移。尼尼微的劫掠使亞述的神像、寶物與大量泥板流散到巴比倫與其他城市，尼尼微的城區在火災之後被放棄，泥板被埋在坍塌的填土層中，卻也因此保存完好；今天靠這些泥板重建了亞述王朝的世系、戰爭年表、王室文書與文學作品，亞述巴尼拔圖書館的規模之所以在學界無與倫比，正源於此。19世紀流入歐洲的亞述浮雕與青銅器，則直接在維多利亞時代塑造了公眾對「亞述」這個名字的想象，也影響了當時「文明對野蠻」這一整套論述的走向。

第四層是文學與記憶。巴比倫編年史在描述城破後的分配時提到一名「哈提之地的王」被分給聯軍，學者多認為與以色列王國被俘的記錄有關；巴比倫把亞述的神像運回自己的神廟，則在宗教上宣告了新秩序的合法。從文本傳統看，《那鴻書》以尼尼微為主要對象寫出它的傾覆，《約拿書》則把尼尼微寫成一座能悔改的城，兩者把一座已不存在於當代政治地圖上的城市，變成了後世兩千年反覆使用的象徵。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the siege was the end of the Assyrian empire. After the fall of Nineveh all that remained of Assyria as an independent political entity was Harran, and Harran too passed to Babylonia in 609 BC while the royal house migrated west to Egypt. From then on there was no independent Assyria anywhere in the Near East, until in the nineteenth century Layard and Rassam dug the walls and the palace out of the mounds at Mosul and the scholarly world learned that such an empire had existed at all. The second layer of consequence is the reordering of power in Mesopotamia. The purpose of the Babylonian-Median alliance was the joint destruction of Assyria, but the division of the spoils sowed the seed of the split: Babylon took Harran and the lower Mesopotamian west, the Medes took the uplands to the north-east, the two collided around Harran in 609 BC, and in 605 BC Babylon defeated the Medes at Cadytia. The alliance broke for good, most of the former Assyrian land passed to Babylonia, and the Assyrian province of the age of Nebuchadnezzar was in this way converted into a Babylonian province. The administrative tradition of Assyria, its cuneiform documentary system and its military organisation did not perish with it; they were absorbed wholesale by the successor states, which is the usual pattern when an empire dies: the machine of government is taken apart and reassembled. The third layer concerns the preservation and the transfer of knowledge and craft. The sack of Nineveh scattered the gods, the treasure and a great mass of tablets across Babylonia and other cities, and the city was abandoned after the fire, so that the tablets were buried in the collapse fill, which is exactly why they survive in such unusual quantity. It is from them that the Assyrian king lists, the war annals, the royal correspondence and the literature of the court have been reconstructed, and it is from them that the Library of Ashurbanipal derives its unrival standing in scholarship. The Assyrian reliefs and bronzes that flowed into Europe in the nineteenth century shaped the Victorian public's imagination of the name Assyria and had their effect on the whole contemporary discourse of civilisation against barbarism. The fourth layer is literary and mnemonic. The Babylonian chronicle, in describing the distribution after the city's fall, mentions a king of the land of Khatti being allotted to the victors, which many scholars connect with the record of the capture of the king of Israel; and the transfer of the Assyrian gods back to the Babylonian sanctuaries proclaimed the legitimacy of a new order in religious terms. In the textual tradition, the Book of Nahum takes Nineveh as its principal object and sings of its overthrow, while the Book of Jonah makes it a city capable of repentance, and the two together turned a city that had vanished from every contemporary political map into a symbol used and reused for two thousand years afterwards.
result:
結果有四層。第一層是戰役本身：公元前612年塔穆茲月，聯軍在圍城約三個月之後攻破西城牆，從缺口湧入尼尼微，王宮與城區被焚，神像、金銀與財物被掠走，阿舒爾-巴尼拔二世不在城中，帶著王室殘部逃往哈蘭。巴比倫編年史記下這一戰的收束：城被毀，掠物被帶走，亞述王脫身。前609年，哈蘭陷落，哈蘭的守軍與王室成員被清剿，亞述王朝在美索不達米亞的統治從此完全結束，末代王的餘生在埃及度過，一個曾經獨霸兩河流域、四出征伐的王朝，連同它的國號，在正史上被劃上句號。

第二層是戰利品的分配：亞述的疆域由巴比倫與米底瓜分。前612至前609年間，聯軍的共同體維持著一種脆弱的平衡；前609年兩方在哈蘭附近交鋒，前605年拿波那帕沙在戰役中死去，繼任的阿米爾-馬爾杜克在卡爾迪希擊敗米底，巴比倫把上美索不達米亞與亞述行省收入囊中，米底退回伊朗高原。此後數百年，兩河流域的霸權歸於巴比倫，再歸於波斯，亞述的廢墟之下則是層層疊疊的後來城市。

第三層是亞述這套軍事技術的傳播。城牆技術、城防工程、鐵器生產與文書行政並沒有隨城燒毀，它們被聯軍分別繼承：巴比倫人拿走了神像與檔案，也拿走了亞述式的文書格式與行省制度；米底人帶走了亞述的騎兵戰術與後來居上的政權形式。甚至在亞述自己的故地，亞述的城名、行省名與王表都繼續在文書中沿用了很多年，只是換了寫下它們的國王。

第四層是歷史定位。尼尼微的陷落是前7世紀末那次聯盟反攻的高潮，也是古代近東第一次出現「帝國被聯軍當場摧毀」的完整案例；後來希臘人、波斯人、希伯來人與阿拉伯人講起這一役時，敘事重心都落在廢墟、暴行與神罰的意象上，而它真正的技術內容——攻城坡道、地道夜襲、水渠防守與列盾矛陣——要到十九世紀的考古與二十世紀的文本研究，才被重新拼回完整。
resultEn: The outcome has four layers. The first is the battle itself. In the month of Tammuz of 612 BC, after a siege of about three months, the coalition broke the western wall and poured into Nineveh through the breach; the palace and the city were burned, the gods, the gold and silver and the treasure were carried off, and Ashur-uballit II was not in the city: he escaped with the remnants of the court to Harran. The Babylonian chronicle sets down the conclusion of the fight in its own terse way: the city was destroyed, the booty was taken away, the Assyrian king got clear. In 609 BC Harran fell, the garrison and the royal house there were liquidated, and Assyrian rule in Mesopotamia came to an end for good; the last king spent what remained of his life in Egypt, and a dynasty that had once lorded it over the two rivers and campaigned to every horizon was closed off in the official record, name and all. The second layer is the division of the spoils: the Assyrian territories were shared between Babylon and Media. From 612 to 609 BC the coalition held together in a fragile balance; in 609 the two parties clashed near Harran, in 605 Nabopolassar was killed in a campaign, and his successor Amel-Marduk defeated the Medes at Cadytia, after which Babylon took upper Mesopotamia and the Assyrian province into its own hands and the Medes withdrew to the Iranian plateau. For the centuries that followed, the overlordship of Mesopotamia belonged to Babylon and then to Persia, and under the ruins of Nineveh lay the layered cities of the successors. The third layer is the transmission of Assyrian military craft. The city's fortification technique, its siege engineering, its iron production and its documentary administration did not burn with the city; the victors inherited them piece by piece. The Babylonians took the gods and the archives, and with them the Assyrian formats of writing and the Assyrian system of provincial government; the Medes took the cavalry art of Assyria and, later, the form of government that would in time overshadow them. Even in Assyria's own country the Assyrian city names, province names and king list went on being used in the documents for many years to come, only with a different king writing them down. The fourth layer is the historical position of the event. The fall of Nineveh was the climax of the counter-offensive that began in the late seventh century BC, and the first fully recorded case in the ancient Near East of an empire being destroyed on the field by a coalition. When the Greeks, the Persians, the Hebrews and the Arabs told the story afterwards, the weight of their narrative fell on ruins, violence and divine punishment; the real technical content of the siege, the ramp, the tunnel assault by night, the defence of the aqueduct and the shield-and-spear line, was not put back together until the archaeology of the nineteenth century and the textual research of the twentieth.
